doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: His father's teaching of country bands, and the grandsons' lessons
summary: Discussion of how the father taught bands at plantations and parishes and taught the grandsons Percy and Earl; Willie E. says he stopped clarinet and married at 23.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: That's strange. Did your father ever play in any dance bands, or did he just teach most of the time?
I used to teach bands, they used to teach bands at different kinds.

I heard he taught like that at Magnolia Plantation and those places. All in the country, the court, the reserve and all other places. St. John and St. Charles Paragraph. He used to bring bands in here for St. Patrick's Den and all those big praises to have here. Did he ever play much himself or did he just teach most of the time?
He teached them. He had time. He teached them. He was one, seven, three years old.

I mean, he was like a girl and playing solos on the trumpets and different concepts and things like that. He had us playing in this room here from Goddard's Wimps. The piano was over there. I didn't hear. He had it. When I wasn't playing the bass, I was playing the piano.
Ah, yeah. Did you play the bass with a bow?

Yes, with a bow. Three string bass. Three string. I think it was a G, D, and A spread. And he keep putting in the Killing Melody Black plan. That's the first book. He had all kinds of orchestration music. He taught all his grandsons. He was all happy to say. You studied with your grandfather then, Willis? All of us. Percy and Earl.
Yeah, I helped Percy too. Percy was playing drums. You know he was playing trumpet? Yeah, he started on drums.

Yes, I remember. I never heard him on drums. Other people have told me that. They used to hear him on drums. Yeah, I used to get a little job, you know. Get a little work in the cinema. When did you stop playing, Mr. Humphrey? How late did you work on it?

I stopped playing clarinet at the 23-year-old. Frank Lewis taught me. He showed the keys. I was married at 23-year-old. I was married at 23-year-old. I was first to play music at the 19-year-old. I was first to play music at the 19-year-old.
Yeah, I finished here in 19-year-old. Yeah, I finished here in 19-year-old.
